title.narrative: Mekong Australia Partnership Phase 1 - Laos Economic Resilience Fund

description.narrative: Mekong Australia Partnership (MAP) Economic Resilience pillar funded activities in Laos are providing targeted support across a range of its priority areas, including supporting Public Financial Management reforms. Building capacity in this area is equipping decision-makers with the tools they need to make well informed and timely policy decisions that will impact the long-term prosperity of Laos. Specific areas of engagement include State Owned Enterprise reform, tax administration and debt management, and better management of the education budget.

participating-org.narrative: AUSTRALIA - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: As part of the Public Financial Management for Stability program in Laos, the World Bank provided technical support to the Lao Government, leading to the adoption of the Prime Minister’s Decree on Budget Formulation in August 2023. The Decree strengthened the authorising environment for ministers to coordinate and jointly prepare state budget policy statements. A notable policy reform is the reversal of a Value Added Tax reduction from 7 per cent back to 10 per cent through a Presidential Decree to enhance domestic revenue mobilisation and help Laos raise an estimated additional one per cent of GDP.

Laos is committed to the SDGs and national development planning; however, its statistical system remains constrained by outdated methodologies, limited disaggregation, and low data quality. These gaps undermine evidence-based decision making and hinder the effective design, implementation, and monitoring of inclusive development policies. ‍ Through the Strengthening Gender and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Data and Analysis program, Australia is transforming how Laos collects and uses disaggregated data. In 2020, only 37.7% of gender-relevant indicators were available for SDG monitoring. By 2024, this had significantly improved, with 53 of 257 indicators in the Voluntary National Review (VNR) featuring GEDSI disaggregated data which is more than double the 2017 figure. A key achievement was the development of a manual on GEDSI data and analysis with regards to development outcomes, guiding the integration of sex, disability, and ethnicity data into censuses and surveys. ‍ To ensure sustainability, the program supported the Lao Statistics Bureau in establishing its first ever Gender Statistics Division. This dedicated in-house unit enhances institutional capacity and embeds gender and social inclusion data into national statistical systems. By strengthening data collection and analysis, the program is driving more inclusive, evidence-based policymaking and supporting Laos’ long-term commitment to equitable development

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Laos’ public financial management program supported by the World Bank and Mekong-Australia Partnership enabled the rollout of new VAT rules for digital suppliers. Over 2,800 stakeholders were reached through nation-wide dissemination, helping the Ministry of Finance secure over USD2.5 million in new VAT revenue from over 30 registered major digital platforms. This intervention directly responds to Laos’ low tax-to-GDP ratio, which remains a key constraint to fiscal sustainability. These efforts not only broadened the tax base but also created sustainable fiscal space to fund national priorities and build a more resilient economy for Laos.

The creation of a Treasury Single Account in Laos in July 2024 through a public financial management program (supported by the World Bank and Mekong-Australia Partnership), has enabled the Government of Laos to centralise and control public revenues through the central bank. Combined with a new Chart of Accounts (part of the Lao Integrated Financial Management Information System) and aligned to international standards, these reforms lay the groundwork for budgeting and real-time fiscal oversight which are the foundations of a transparent and accountable public financial system. This will help address a long-standing need to address public cash management systems to support the government's ability to respond to shocks and manage rising debt levels. Improved liquidity management has already contributed to exchange rate stabilisation and helped curb inflation, which remains a key priority for the Government of Laos. These reforms are increasing the transparency of the public sector and helping to rebuild public trust and international confidence in Laos’ fiscal governance.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Through the Public Financial Management (PFM) for Stability Laos program, the World Bank provided technical support to Government of Laos which led to the adoption of the Prime Minister’s Decree on Budget Formulation. The adoption of the Decree has enabled a strong authorising environment for ministers to coordinate and jointly prepare the state budget policy statement. A notable policy reform has been the reversal of the Value Added Tax (VAT) from 7 per cent back to 10 per cent through a presidential decree to enhance domestic revenue mobilisation and help Laos raise 1 per cent of GDP. Through the Strengthening Gender and Social Inclusion Data and Analysis in the Lao PDR Statistical System program, the Asia Development Bank supported improvements in the Government of Laos’ capacity for Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) data collection, monitoring, analytics, and reporting by providing technical assistance to the country’s statistics agency. This activity saw improvements in Laos’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) reporting by increasing the availability of the statistics agency’s data disaggregation (by sex, ethnicity and other forms of disaggregation), and the embedding of GEDSI methodologies into the agency’s statistical reports, as well as their survey and questionnaire designs.
